synopsis: Zeus, supreme chairman of the Council of Valhalla, announces to the gods twelve of the thirteen fighters set to participate in Ragnarok--and is met with the dissenting voices of those who were not chosen. However, Zeus has foreseen this, and immediately declares the holding of another tournament to decide the final spot on the Ragnarok lineup, one which will break the taboo on gods fighting one another. Thus begins the "Revelation" of the untold side of Record of Ragnarok!

title: Cheori Eopseoseo Geurae
synopsis: Ha-Ji, who tutored students as a side job, ends up tutoring Il-Do, a wealthy student retaking the college entrance exam. One day, she receives shocking news from her younger sister. “Sis, did you know... Il-Do is actually a junior of mine at university?” It turns out that Il-Do, whom she thought was a student retaking the college entrance exam, is actually a junior at Korea University who has already been accepted. From the day his true identity is revealed, Il-Do’s meticulous schemes and relentless obsession begin to slowly tighten their grip on Ha-Ji’s life. (Source: Naver, translated)

title: Changsheng Zhi Nüjiang Xing
synopsis: General Heyan met her end through betrayal, only to be reborn as a frail maiden. Vowing to reclaim all she lost, she returned to the barracks and took up arms once more under a new identity, determined to earn a marquis title and strike fear into the Nine Provinces. Along the way, she reunited with her formidable foe from a past life—a wolfish young general. Hand in hand, they marched onto the battlefield together, forging the legend of the Twin Generals. Amidst tangled threads of love and hate, and the treacherous web of power struggles, witness how this woman of valor earns her marquis title and strikes fear into the hearts of all under heaven. (Source: Tencent, translated)

title: Lazy Girl Momogusa
titleNative: 桃草さんがものぐさすぎる!!
synopsis: Souji Hataki is an ordinary high school boy who has just landed the perfect new part-time job as a housekeeper for the house of Momogusa. What’s so significant about that? It just so happens to be the home of the most beautiful girl in school! Perfect, pretty, and popular, Momogusa-san is amazing at everything she does and now Hataki will have a chance to see her in her element. But, he quickly learns something shocking: Momogusa is incredibly lazy at home! The moment she’s home from school, she seems to transform into a totally different version of herself and even expects to be pampered! Somehow she grows fond of Hataki and even begins to let him pamper her. Could this be the start of some sort of relationship or is Hataki just a glorified manservant? (Source: Seven Seas Entertainment)

synopsis: The love between brother and sister. The love between man and woman. That which is most forbidden is most unyielding. The two sons and five daughters of the Shiunji family shine like brilliant gems, each with intelligence and beauty in equal measure. And with the pedigree of their wealthy father behind them, how could they not be the talk of the town? Eldest son Arata has spent his life being tossed around by the whims of his colorful sisters, yet a little teasing won’t stop him from valuing his family over anything and anyone else. But when his youngest sister turns fifteen, their father reveals a long-hidden secret of the Shiunji “siblings” and knocks Arata’s world off its axis… (Source: Yen Press) Note: The manga is getting their chapters published first on Miyajima's Fanbox account, and then some days later on the Young Animal magazine from Hakusensha editorial.

synopsis: Fonons. Essential components of all matter on planet Auldrant. Ages ago, a new type of fonon was discovered—the Seventh Fonon. Its discovery threw humanity into chaos, for if one could use the Seventh Fonon, one could learn the future. Wars over the Seventh Fonon raged across the lands, ending only when the miasma—a poison from within the planet—covered the entire world. This is when Yulia appeared. A fonist skilled in prophecy, Yulia saw thousands of years into the future and foresaw a way to seal away the miasma. With the guidance of her prophecies, humanity sealed the miasma deep within the planet. Over two thousand years passed. The world is ruled by Yulia's prophecy, known as the Score. People believe in the coming “unprecedented prosperity” promised in the Score, never straying from the path set forth in the Score which will lead them to that prosperity. They look to the Score as revealed by the Order of Lorelei, the religion Yulia founded, and hold that the greatest virtue is to follow the Score faithfully. synopsis: Gaku is the son of former Japanese national volleyball star Kei Shishiya. Through middle school, he's played as his team's ace hitter, though part of him wonders if that's a title he earned, or one he was simply given. One day, Kei meets Noboru, a generational volleyball talent with a monstrous spiking arm, and vows to turn him into the next national standout. In the wake of that choice, Gaku realizes he can't play the style his father demands, but swears he'll defeat both Kei and Noboru with a game that's entirely his own. (Source: K MANGA)

title: Toumei na Yoru ni Kakeru Kimi to, Me ni Mienai Koi wo Shita.
titleRomaji: Toumei na Yoru ni Kakeru Kimi to, Me ni Mienai Koi wo Shita.
titleNative: 透明な夜に駆ける君と、目に見えない恋をした。
synonyms: Love Unseen Beneath the Clear Night Sky
synopsis: On an April night in Tokyo, still too early for fireworks, university student Kakeru Sorano meets a woman named Koharu Fuyutsuki. She is a beautiful girl who stands out from the crowd, laughs a lot, and exudes a warmth that contrasts sharply with Kakeru's own introversion. But there was something Kakeru didn't know at first—she can't see. Unlike Kakeru, Koharu hasn't given up on anything, even with her blindness. She attends university daily, shows interest in clubs, makes friends—and dreams of launching fireworks one day. Kakeru wonders why, when she can't see them...but maybe it doesn't matter. And maybe he can start moving forward, too, for the girl who's always been by his side (Source: Yen Press)
